newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Christopher in Mideast stressing urgency of talks.
newsitem.headline: Christopher in Mideast stressing urgency of talks.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher arrived in the Middle East to urge Israelis and Palestinians to reach swift and significant results in resumed peace talks on Sunday.

He arrived 11 hours before the scheduled start of negotiations in the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip -- the outcome of last week's emergency White House summit spurred by clashes and gunbattles unprecedented in three years of peacemaking.

On his way to Israel, Christopher said he would remind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat at separate meetings on Sunday of their promise in Washington to become personally involved if progress wasn't made in the lower-level talks.

The Gaza talks, with the participation of Christopher's Middle East envoy Dennis Ross, will centre on an Israeli redeployment from Hebron delayed since March by Islamic suicide bombings that killed 59 people and by Israeli security concerns.

The city, holy to Moslems and Jews as the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham, is the only one of seven West Bank towns in a 1995 peace deal yet to be given Palestinian self-rule -- and the only one where Jews live among Arabs.

Christopher told reporters flying with him he wanted to stress "the importance of significant progress, the urgency of it and especially a reminder of their commitment that they would become personally involved if progress wasn't made."

It remained to be seen how the two sides would reconcile differences over Hebron and other issues such as demands by Israel for tougher security arrangements and by Palestinians for easing of restrictions.

It was largely quiet early on Sunday in the West Bank and Gaza. Israel said it lifted an 11-day-old curfew on Hebron on Sunday. Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai said he hoped to further lower tensions, ordering that tanks pull back some from Palestinian towns and cities.
Netanyahu views Israeli-PLO peace accords as fundamentally flawed but promises to see the Hebron redeployment through as an international commitment.

His top adviser Dore Gold told Israel Radio that although Israel did not commit to a deadline on Hebron, Netanyahu and his team made clear in Washington that they wanted to complete the negotiations "as quickly as possible".
Gold said Israel viewed the U.S. role as that of a "facilitator" helping the negotiators without taking their place.
The Palestinians -- and the United States -- have demanded a deadline for the pullback.
"We will not renegotiate or reopen agreements signed. We will not agree to modifications of agreements signed," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters.
Fifty-eight Palestinians and 15 Israelis died in violence that erupted after Netanyahu opened a new entrance to an archaeological tunnel near a Moslem shrine in Jerusalem.
Palestinians said they were frustrated at the slow pace of peace moves.

Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring was due to head for Israel and Gaza also on Sunday on a peace mission ordered by European leaders frustrated and angry at being cut out of U.S.-brokered peace efforts.
Christopher seemed cool to a direct European role, saying "any major change in the bilateral character of these negotiations is not likely to take place."

Officials said they did not know whether Spring, whose country currently holds the rotating EU presidency, would visit the Palestinian Authority's Orient House offices in Arab East Jerusalem -- a move that would anger Israel as reflecting support for Palestinian claims to the holy city.

In Jerusalem on Saturday night, thousands of Israelis took to the streets to protest at Netanyahu's handling of peace talks and to mourn Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin, shot dead 11 months ago by a right-wing Israeli angered by his peace policies.
"We did not come here to hate," Rabin's son, Yuval, told the crowd. "We came here to remember."
